newsitem.title: HONG KONG: China pharmaceutical firms seek listings - papers.
newsitem.headline: China pharmaceutical firms seek listings - papers.

text.p: Shanghai-listed North China Pharmaceutical Group Corp has applied to China's securities regulator for an overseas listing, preferably in Tokyo, the Hong Kong Economic Times reported on Tuesday.

"North China's first choice is Tokyo and it hopes to raise two billion yuan for company expansion," the Economic Times quoted Han Lixin, director of the State Pharmaceutical Administration's economic management bureau, as saying.

Han said five Chinese pharmaceutical firms are applying to the China Securities Regulatory Commission (CSRC) to float shares on overseas or China's hard-currency B share markets to finance their expansion, the South China Morning Post reported.
"The enterprises do not care whether they are allowed to issue H shares abroad, or B shares locally," the Post quoted Han as saying. "What matters is that they need money for expansion."
H shares are listed in Hong Kong, while B shares are listed in Shenzhen or Shanghai and reserved for foreign investors.

In addition to North China in Shijiazhuang, the firms include Northeast Pharmaceutical Group Corp in Shenyang, which wants to issue B shares, Sanjiu Enterprise in Shenzhen, Harbin Pharmaceutical and a pharmaceutical group in Guangzhou which will merge with other companies, the Post added.

Han said the applications were subject to regulatory approval and he was confident penicillin maker North China Pharmacetuical would be included in the upcoming fourth batch of overseas listing candidates to be approved by Beijing.
There are 21 Chinese companies with H shares listed in Hong Kong and another two have listings in New York.
North China's vice-general manager Lian Fazhe told the Economic Times he did not rule out issuing shares on other exchanges if the Tokyo listing did not materialise.

Shanghai brokers said in September that listings by Chinese companies on the Tokyo market next year was unlikely because of opposition from Japan's Finance Ministry, but that listings in London was probable.
A Memorandum of Understanding (MOU) to allow the listing of Chinese companies was due to be signed soon between the CSRC and the London Stock Exchange, they said.
More than 80 percent of North China's 1995 turnover of 2.04 billion yuan was from the manufacturing and sale of penicillin.
Shijiazhuang-based North China, which is listed in the domestic Shanghai A share market, posted a net profit of 320 million yuan in calendar year 1995, the Economic Times said.
